title: PrairieRx Plan Assignment Rule
content:
**Policy statement.** The Pharmacy Benefit plan follows the member's plan eligibility category through the plan category map of the PrairieRx plans. Holding an active LTSS Service Coordination care enrollment with a nursing facility residence overrides the map: such a member holds PrairieRx Long-Term Care, except that a Prairie Ridge Dual Complete member always holds PrairieRx Dual Wrap because Part D pays first. Holding PrairieRx Dual Wrap and any other pharmacy plan at the same time is impossible; the two are mutually exclusive.

### Order of precedence

1. A Prairie Ridge Dual Complete member holds PrairieRx Dual Wrap, whatever else is true.
2. Any other member with an active LTSS Service Coordination care enrollment and a nursing facility residence holds PrairieRx Long-Term Care.
3. Every other member holds the PrairieRx plan whose category list contains the member's plan eligibility category.

### Decision table

| Plan eligibility category is Prairie Ridge Dual Complete | Active LTSS Service Coordination care enrollment with nursing facility residence | PrairieRx plan held |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | PrairieRx Dual Wrap |
| Yes | No | PrairieRx Dual Wrap |
| No | Yes | PrairieRx Long-Term Care |
| No | No | The plan mapped to the member's category |

### Points of judgement

*Does a nursing facility resident with LTSS Service Coordination who is a Prairie Ridge Dual Complete member move to PrairieRx Long-Term Care?* No. The Dual Complete member always holds PrairieRx Dual Wrap, because Medicare Part D pays first.

*Can a member hold PrairieRx Dual Wrap together with another PrairieRx plan?* No. PrairieRx Dual Wrap and any other pharmacy plan are mutually exclusive.

*Where does the plan come from for a member with neither condition?* From the member's plan eligibility category, read through the category list of each PrairieRx plan.
